nodes.text: The core ideas of diffusion can be derived without SDEs, ELBOs, Langevin dynamics, the VAE framework, or even the notion of a score, requiring only basic probability, calculus, linear algebra, and multivariate Gaussians.
nodes.evidence: for the core ideas we will not need any SDEs, Evidence-Based-Lower-Bounds (ELBOs), Langevin dynamics, or even the notion of a score

nodes.text: Unlike most diffusion tutorials, the presentation takes neither a Variational Auto Encoder (VAE) nor a Stochastic Differential Equations (SDE) approach.
nodes.evidence: Unlike most tutorials on this subject, we take neither a Variational Auto Encoder (VAE) nor an Stochastic Differential Equations (SDE) approach

nodes.text: The key insight of diffusion is that learning to reverse each small intermediate noising step is easier than learning to sample from the target distribution in one step, because adjacent distributions p_{t-1} and p_t are already close.
nodes.evidence: The key insight of diffusion is, learning to reverse each intermediate step can be easier than learning to sample from the target distribution in one step

nodes.text: Gaussian diffusion defines a forward process that successively adds independent small-scale Gaussian noise to data (x_{t+1} = x_t + eta_t, eta_t ~ N(0, sigma^2)), transforming the data distribution into a nearly Gaussian distribution at large step count T.
nodes.evidence: construct a sequence of random variables x1, x2, ... by successively adding independent Gaussian noise ... xt+1 := xt + eta_t, eta_t ~ N(0, sigma^2)

nodes.text: For small per-step noise sigma, the reverse conditional distribution p(x_{t-1} | x_t) is itself approximately Gaussian with known variance, so only its mean needs to be learned (Fact 1 / Claim 1).
nodes.evidence: For small sigma, and the Gaussian diffusion process ... the conditional distribution p(xt-1 | xt) is itself close to Gaussian

nodes.text: Learning the mean of the reverse conditional reduces the problem of sampling from an arbitrary distribution to a standard regression (denoising) problem, since E[x_{t-1} | x_t] is the minimizer of a squared-error regression loss.
nodes.evidence: we have reduced the problem of learning to sample from an arbitrary distribution to the standard problem of regression

nodes.text: A reverse sampler is defined abstractly as a (possibly stochastic) function F_t such that if x_t ~ p_t then F_t(x_t) is distributed exactly as p_{t-1}, an abstraction not specific to Gaussian noise and extendable to discrete domains.
nodes.evidence: a reverse sampler for step t is a potentially stochastic function Ft such that if xt ~ pt, then the marginal distribution of Ft(xt) is exactly pt-1

nodes.text: The DDPM stochastic reverse sampler outputs x_{t-Delta t} = mu_{t-Delta t}(x_t) + N(0, sigma_q^2 Delta t), where mu is the learned conditional expectation E[x_{t-Delta t} | x_t].
A heuristic derivation via Bayes' rule and Taylor expansion shows the score of the marginal appears in the reverse process mean: E[x_{t-Delta t} | x_t = z] = z + sigma_q^2 Delta t * grad log p_t(z).
nodes.evidence: = z + (sigma_q^2 dt) grad log pt(z), where pt is the marginal distribution of xt

nodes.text: Flow Matching can be thought of as a generalization of diffusion (and of the deterministic DDIM sampler) that offers additional flexibility, including rectified flows / linear flows.
nodes.evidence: Section 4 covers the closely-related topic of Flow Matching, which can be thought of as a generalization of diffusion that offers additional flexibility (including what are called rectified flows or linear flows)

nodes.text: DDIM is a deterministic reverse sampler, and it can be interpreted as a special case of flow matching.
nodes.evidence: the DDIM sampler (Section 3), which is deterministic, and the family of flow-matching models (Section 4), which can be thought of as a generalization of DDIM

nodes.text: Variance is controlled by scaling each increment's noise variance by Delta t = 1/T (sigma = sigma_q sqrt(Delta t)) so the terminal distribution p_T has variance sigma_q^2 independent of the number of discretization steps T.
nodes.evidence: we need to scale the variance of each increment by dt = 1/T ... This choice ensures that the variance of pT is always sigma_q^2, regardless of T

nodes.text: There is no canonical reverse sampler for a given set of marginals because many joint distributions (couplings) are consistent with the same marginals, leaving freedom to choose the most convenient one.
nodes.evidence: There is therefore no canonical reverse sampler for a given set of marginals {pt} - we are free to chose whichever coupling is most convenient.
